notes: Wall clock 2.62h against an estimate of 2.5h looks near-exact, and that is a coincidence worth not believing. Active engineering was ~1.1h, a 2.3x over-estimate; the remaining ~1.5h was blocked on the gh OAuth token lacking the workflow scope, which needed a browser login the agent could not perform. Two errors in opposite directions happened to cancel. Recorded as partial for exactly that reason: scoring this as an accurate prediction would teach the calibrator the wrong lesson twice over.

Under-estimated by ~2.1x on the measure the estimate was stated in: 2.0h of active engineering predicted, ~4.2h spent. Active time is the sum of four working windows bounded by commit timestamps, each extended backwards by the reading that preceded its first commit; it is an estimate of an estimate's error and nothing here measures keystrokes. The blocked figure is not usefully comparable to OUT-0001's: the phase ran across four sessions ended by credit exhaustion, so the 68.5h is elapsed time containing nights rather than measured waiting, recorded only so the wall clock reconciles. Compare active against active. Where the estimate went wrong is legible: it priced the records and the schema, which cost about what was predicted, and did not price the four store test modules that make them trustworthy - roughly 1,700 lines and over half the engineering. Direction is the opposite of OUT-0001's, in a different work class, at n=1 each: exactly the shape of data a human over-reads and BiasDetective refuses to answer on below n=5.

Under-estimated by ~1.24x on the measure the estimate was stated in: 4.5h of active engineering predicted, ~5.6h spent. Same methodology as OUT-0002 and the same caveat - three working windows bounded by commit timestamps (1.25h, 2.35h, 2.0h), each extended backwards by the work that preceded its first commit, so this is an estimate of an estimate's error and nothing here measures keystrokes. The third window's lead-in is the least certain figure in the record because it precedes any commit: synthesis.py and its 58 tests were written before the first commit of that session. Blocked time is elapsed time containing a night, recorded only so the wall clock reconciles; compare active against active. Scored close rather than exact because the scope was not the scope that was priced, and it moved in both directions. Not built: the bounded repair loop named in the estimate's subject, now in BACKLOG.md with its reason - its shape is decided by what the first agents actually get back, and writing it now would be guessing at a failure distribution nobody has measured. Substituted: the per-agent mock response library for the five named agents became a schema-driven synthesiser that names no agent at all, which covers those five and every later one, and which is a better answer to the same requirement rather than a cheaper one. Built beyond the estimate: the boundary test, the provider factory, RecordingAnthropicProvider, and doctor making a real offline call. Also cheaper than priced: the estimate included two ADRs that turned out to already exist, written in Phase 0. The scope correction OUT-0002 asked for worked. EST-0003 priced roughly 2,200 production lines and roughly 3,000 test lines as line items; the actual is 2,246 production and 2,566 test - the production figure is close to exact, and the test figure is short by about the repair loop that was not built. That is the first estimate in this corpus whose conditions can be checked against the artifact rather than argued about. Third work class, third direction of error at n=1 each: over 2.3x, under 2.1x, under 1.24x. Still below BiasDetective's threshold, and still not a reason to correct EST-0004.

Over-estimated by ~1.3x on the measure the estimate was stated in: 5.5h of active engineering predicted, ~4.2h spent. First over-estimate since Phase 0, and the first outcome in this corpus whose active figure cannot be bounded from both ends. Phase 3 ran across two sessions and the first ended on a five-hour session limit WITHOUT a final commit, so its length is bounded below by commit timestamps (22:49-23:35 on 2026-08-16, plus a lead-in of context reload and planning and a tail of uncommitted work) and above by the session limit, with nothing recording where inside that range the work stopped. OUT-0002 and OUT-0003 could bound their windows from both ends; this one cannot, and 4.2h should be read as the midpoint of a defensible range rather than as a measurement. The second window is tighter: 10:58-11:21 of commits plus a short lead-in and a close-out for the PR, CI watch, merge, tag and report. Blocked time is elapsed time containing a night, recorded only so the wall clock reconciles; compare active against active. Scored close rather than exact because the scope moved in one direction sharply. The scope correction OUT-0002 demanded worked again on tests and failed on production: EST-0004 priced roughly 2,600 test lines against an actual 2,826, close to exact for the third phase running, and roughly 1,900 production lines against an actual 3,740 - nearly 2x under. The reason is legible and is the lesson for EST-0005: the conditions priced 'the synthetic corpus generator' as one line item, and it became five modules and 1,301 lines with its own format, its own validation and its own tests. Everything else in the phase landed close to a line-item reading. That is a better error than Phase 1's, which under-priced the tests that make a feature trustworthy - a category mistake; this is an ordinary estimation miss on one named component, and it is visible at all only because the estimate priced line items. Conditions that were checkable all held: no migration was needed (schema still at version 3), no live API call was made, the structured-output layer and its repair loop were built inside the phase as deferred from Phase 2, the corpus generator was built inside the phase rather than deferred to Phase 10, and the segmenter's deterministic floor was built before its LLM path. Built beyond the estimate: praxis ingest and praxis corpus generate, the re-ingestion lookup in the store, cli_tables.py, and ordinals_in in the Phase 2 synthesiser - the last of which was necessary rather than optional, because without it every synthesised grouping referred to a block that was never offered and the code path honouring a good grouping would never have run offline. Fourth work class, fourth outcome, and the directions still disagree: over 2.3x, under 2.1x, under 1.24x, over 1.3x, n = 1 each. Still below BiasDetective's threshold of 5, and still not a reason to correct EST-0005.

Over-estimated by ~2.2x on the measure the estimate was stated in: 6.0h of active engineering predicted, ~2.75h spent. Second outcome in agent-implementation and the second over-estimate in that class, which makes it the first work class in this corpus with a consistent direction rather than a single point - still n = 2, still below BiasDetective's threshold of 5, and still not a reason to correct EST-0006. Active is the sum of three session windows, and unlike OUT-0004 every one of them is bounded from both ends by commits. Session 1: 01:30 (EST-0005, logged before any phase 4 file existed) to 01:58 on 2026-08-18, 0.47h of commits plus roughly 0.3h of lead-in reading NEXT.md and writing the estimate - the prompt library, migration 004, the span offering, DecisionScout and DecisionStructurer all landed inside it. Session 2: 14:41 to 15:28 the same day, 0.78h plus a short lead-in - the citation gate, AssumptionExtractor, the extraction pipeline and praxis/eval/. Session 3: roughly 03:05 to 04:00 on 2026-08-21 - the eval tests, the two CLI commands, the docs and the close-out. Blocked time is ~72h against 16h predicted, and the gap is not an estimation error in any useful sense: it is two nights and two days of wall clock between sessions, recorded only so the elapsed figure reconciles. Compare active against active. Scored partial rather than close because 2.2x is outside the band OUT-0004's 1.3x sat in, and because the scope moved underneath the estimate in a way the hours hide: EST-0005 priced roughly 1,650 production lines across its named components and 3,799 landed. Where the estimate was right: the four-line-item pricing of the eval harness, which is the correction OUT-0004 bought, came in at 998 production lines against roughly 550 predicted and 1,205 test lines against 700 - an ordinary miss in both directions rather than the 2x a one-line-item pricing produced last phase, and the ratio between production and tests is the part it got right. Where it was wrong, and this is the lesson for EST-0006: every one of the three agents overran - 299, 412 and 564 production lines against 200, 300 and 350 predicted - and every overrun was in the code that says no. An agent's happy path is one function; its refusal vocabulary is the rest of the file. praxis/agents/citation.py, offering.py and errors.py are 500 lines between them and appear nowhere in the estimate, because when it was written the citation gate was assumed to live inside each agent rather than to be lifted out of the second one that grew it. Conditions that were checkable all held: migration 004 was the only schema change and the schema is at version 4, no live API call was made and no key exists, three ADRs were recorded (0014, 0015, 0016) and the phase report was written, no new FindingKind member was introduced, and the metrics table in docs/reports/phase-4.md is praxis eval's own output pasted in rather than typed. The risk note was right and it is worth saying so: the mock's precision and recall are dominated by the synthesiser, not by the pipeline. praxis/llm/synthesis.py draws a cited ordinal and a quotation independently, so the citation gate refused 29 of 30 claims and every extraction score is 0.0000. The estimate said that would be a reporting outcome rather than a scope change, and it was: the harness is the deliverable, the numbers are a floor, and both the report and praxis eval itself say so beneath the table. Built beyond the estimate: praxis extract and praxis eval, cli_eval.py, the README quickstart, and the ARCHITECTURE.md rewrite for Half A. One commit was reworded on the unmerged branch - c94a2f7 carried a copy of the previous commit's subject while its diff was the whole of praxis/eval/, and a subject that contradicts its own diff is a bad row in a corpus this project intends to read back.
